subject.title: fix(github-copilot): fail closed on unvalidated OAuth enterprise domain

question: Should an unsupported persisted GitHub Copilot OAuth origin hard-fail and require reauthentication, or may OpenClaw intentionally redirect that credential to public GitHub?
rationale: The existing public-GitHub fallback is useful before credentials are issued, but applying it to persisted bearer credentials changes their trust origin; that policy needs explicit security-owner intent.

options.title: Reject and reauthenticate
options.body: Refuse unsupported persisted origins without transmitting either token, and have doctor identify the profile and guide safe reauthentication.

options.title: Redirect to public GitHub
options.body: Retain the fallback only if maintainers explicitly accept public GitHub as the recipient for credentials whose recorded enterprise origin is invalid.

recommendation.title: Reject and reauthenticate
recommendation.body: Refuse unsupported persisted origins without transmitting either token, and have doctor identify the profile and guide safe reauthentication.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history ties this person to persisted auth-store ownership and recent merged work in the same OAuth helper.
